Each unit ends with a 10-mark practice set. Take g = 10 m s⁻² unless stated. Every numerical answer was checked by computer. The marking points are our own, not the official CBSE marking scheme.

Unit 1 of 10: Physical Quantities and SI Units

Key ideas

  • Physical quantity = numerical value × unit (e.g. 5 m).
  • Seven SI base quantities and units: length (metre, m), mass (kilogram, kg), time (second, s), electric current (ampere, A), thermodynamic temperature (kelvin, K), amount of substance (mole, mol), luminous intensity (candela, cd).
  • Supplementary units: plane angle (radian, rad), solid angle (steradian, sr).
  • Derived units are built from base units, e.g. newton = kg m s⁻²; joule = kg m² s⁻²; watt = J s⁻¹.
  • Prefixes: kilo (10³), mega (10⁶), giga (10⁹), milli (10⁻³), micro (10⁻⁶), nano (10⁻⁹), pico (10⁻¹²).
  • Practical units: 1 light year ≈ 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m; 1 AU ≈ 1.496 × 10¹¹ m; 1 Å = 10⁻¹⁰ m; 1 fermi = 10⁻¹⁵ m.

Worked examples

Example 1: Express 1 joule in CGS units (erg). Answer: 1 J = 1 kg m² s⁻² = 10³ g × 10⁴ cm² s⁻² = 10⁷ erg.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) The SI unit of luminous intensity is: (a) lumen (b) candela (c) lux (d) watt. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) How many SI base units are there? Answer: seven.
  3. (2 marks) Express the newton in base units and state one derived unit built from it. Answer: kg m s⁻² (1); e.g. joule = N m (1).
  4. (3 marks) Convert: (i) 5 nm to m; (ii) 3 MW to W; (iii) 2 μs to s. Answer: 5 × 10⁻⁹ m (1); 3 × 10⁶ W (1); 2 × 10⁻⁶ s (1).
  5. (3 marks) A force of 1 N is applied. Express it in dynes, showing working. Answer: 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻² (1) = 10³ g × 10² cm s⁻² (1) = 10⁵ dyne (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Treating temperature in °C as SI. 2. Writing "Kg" or "Sec". 3. Prefix powers wrong. 4. Missing conversion steps. 5. Confusing light year (distance) with time.

Quick recall

  1. Base units? 2. Unit of current? 3. 1 J in erg? 4. Micro? 5. Light year measures?

Answers: 1) Seven. 2) Ampere. 3) 10⁷. 4) 10⁻⁶. 5) Distance.
